controls.title: Triage suspected incidents within four hours
controls.statement: Triage suspected cyber security incidents and determine an appropriate response within four hours where the WA Cyber Security Policy applies.
controls.risk: A slow initial decision could allow an incident to spread and delay the people responsible for containment and external reporting.
controls.scope: Suspected incidents handled by entities subject to the WA Cyber Security Policy.
controls.examine: Compare detection timestamps, triage records, severity decisions and response initiation for sampled suspected incidents.
controls.interview: Ask responders how the four-hour clock starts, who makes the triage decision and how delays are escalated.
controls.test: Trace sampled suspected incidents from first detection to documented triage and response selection.
test_steps: Select suspected incidents from different reporting channels and include cases later confirmed, dismissed and escalated.
Establish the earliest documented awareness time from source records and compare it with triage start, classification, decision and responsible person.
Recalculate elapsed time against the four-hour requirement and verify the record explains pauses, ambiguity and the selected response path.
Inject a controlled suspected-incident report and confirm the on-call process acknowledges, triages and records it before the deadline.
controls.expected: Triage and an appropriate response decision are recorded within four hours of detection.

mappings.basis: Requires incident triage and development of an appropriate response within four hours.

controls.title: Report critical incidents within twelve hours
controls.statement: Report a cyber security incident affecting a critical infrastructure asset as soon as practicable and within twelve hours when it has a significant impact on asset availability.
controls.risk: Late reporting of a serious outage could delay national coordination and assistance while an essential service remains disrupted.
controls.scope: Responsible entities and critical infrastructure assets to which Part 2B of the SOCI Act applies.
controls.examine: Review awareness evidence, availability impact assessment, report content, delivery timestamp and any oral-report follow-up.
controls.interview: Ask legal, operational and incident leaders how significant availability impact is identified and who owns the twelve-hour report.
controls.test: For sampled qualifying incidents, calculate elapsed time from documented awareness to delivery to the relevant Commonwealth body.
test_steps: Select incidents that met or approached the applicable critical-incident threshold and independently confirm the trigger from incident facts.
Establish when the entity became aware of the qualifying incident and obtain the submission receipt or other evidence of delivery to the relevant Commonwealth body.
Recalculate the elapsed time to the initial report, accounting for the exact statutory trigger rather than ticket creation or later confirmation.
Compare the submitted content, follow-up process and contact route with the applicable requirement and record late, incomplete or unsupported non-reporting decisions.
controls.expected: Each qualifying incident was reported as soon as practicable and no later than twelve hours after the entity became aware.

mappings.basis: For an applicable critical infrastructure asset, requires a report when an incident significantly affects availability, as soon as practicable and within 12 hours of awareness.

controls.title: Meet other applicable incident-reporting clocks
controls.statement: Identify every external reporting obligation and meet the shortest applicable clock, including seventy-two hours under the SOCI Act and twenty-four hours under the WA Cyber Security Policy.
controls.risk: An incident could go unreported or be sent to the wrong authority when teams treat different legal and policy clocks as interchangeable.
controls.scope: Incidents with a relevant impact on critical infrastructure and confirmed incidents handled by WA Government entities.
controls.examine: Inspect the obligations register, incident classifications, awareness and detection timestamps, notifications, recipients and evidence of submission.
controls.interview: Ask legal and incident leaders how concurrent obligations are identified and which timestamp starts each clock.
controls.test: Sample incidents under each regime and independently recalculate the applicable deadline and actual reporting time.
test_steps: Create a matrix of reporting regimes, incident classes, triggers, recipients, initial and follow-up deadlines and required content.
Select incidents under each applicable regime and independently determine which triggers and clocks applied from the underlying facts.
Compare calculated deadlines with submission timestamps, receipts and follow-up reports, including cases where several regimes applied to one incident.
Run a tabletop scenario that changes severity and available information over time and verify staff select, update and meet every applicable reporting path.
controls.expected: Each incident is reported to every required recipient within its own trigger and deadline, with the decision trail retained.

mappings.basis: For an applicable critical infrastructure asset, requires reporting of an incident with a relevant impact as soon as practicable and within 72 hours of awareness.
Requires reporting a confirmed cyber security incident to DGov within 24 hours of detection.
Requires suspected or confirmed incidents to be reported to the WA portal within the timeframes set by the Policy.
